results.q: What did you build at IDFC?
results.answer: At IDFC FIRST Bank, I worked as an Application Engineer developing microservices in Go and Python, implementing Kafka retry handling, and tuning SQL queries for large datasets. I also built a Go MCP server with the team to expose banking tools to AI agents and prototyped LLM-based cheque extraction. Additionally, I set up service observability to improve incident resolution times.

results.q: How much faster did your SQL work make the APIs?
results.answer: My SQL tuning work at IDFC FIRST Bank involved optimizing queries and indexes over 50 million records, which resulted in a 42% reduction in API response times.
I did not win the overall Cal Hacks 13.0 competition. My team placed 2nd in the Anthropic's Claude for Public Benefit track for our project, Drigil.

Drigil is a hackathon prototype I built with a three-person team at Cal Hacks 13.0. It uses smart glasses to coach people with intellectual and developmental disabilities through new jobs using their supervisor's voice. We earned 2nd place in Anthropic's Claude for Public Benefit track for this project.

results.answer: I built the pricing and rewards engine for Mend, which uses surge pricing over H3 hexagons to manage coverage. I also wrote the reward rate card, itemized receipts, bounty budgets, and pay-per-visit sponsored campaigns.
